$comment: The pinned source corpus. Every authoritative source keelblock relies on, with the date it was read and a fingerprint of what it said. Memos cite these ids rather than bare URLs, so a claim can always be traced to a specific reading of a specific document. Checked by scripts/check-corpus.mjs.
$why: A URL is not a citation. Documentation changes silently, and a memo citing a page that has since been rewritten looks rigorous while resting on something that no longer exists. Pinning the fingerprint turns 'the source moved' from an invisible event into a detectable one.

tiers.primary: The vendor's own documentation, a standards body, the originating description of a pattern, or the tool's own repository. A claim may rest on this.
tiers.secondary: Practitioner write-ups, vendor-authored comparisons, industry analysis. May orient the search for a primary. A claim may NOT rest on this alone.

sources.title: Changes to HowTo and FAQ rich results
sources.claim: HowTo rich results deprecated and documentation removed; FAQ restricted to well-known authoritative government and health sites; unused structured data causes no harm and has no visible effect.

sources.title: FAQPage structured data
sources.claim: Current documented behavior for FAQPage.

sources.title: Search's I/O 2026 updates
sources.claim: AI Mode at scale; the search interface redesigned for conversational and multimodal input.

sources.title: Parallel Change (Danilo Sato, 2014)
sources.claim: Expand / migrate / contract, with the invariant that existing clients keep consuming the old version until contract.

sources.title: PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX
sources.claim: CREATE INDEX locks the table against writes; CONCURRENTLY avoids that but cannot run inside a transaction block, is unsupported on partitioned tables, takes longer, and leaves an invalid index on failure.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Row Security Policies
sources.claim: USING versus WITH CHECK semantics; FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; BYPASSRLS.

sources.title: Migrating to Cache Components
sources.claim: Dynamic by default; cookies() inside use cache is an error; Suspense or instant=false for runtime data.

sources.title: next-intl with next/root-params
sources.claim: setRequestLocale is deprecated; root-params reads the locale from the route segment and is what permits static rendering.

sources.title: rlsautotest
sources.claim: Generates pgTAP from the policy catalog; states that it proves enforcement matches declaration and cannot know intent; mocks opaque policy functions.

sources.title: boxyhq/saas-starter-kit
sources.claim: Tenant isolation by application guards; zero RLS policies; SSO/audit/webhooks delegated to Jackson, Retraced and Svix.

sources.title: Setting up Server-Side Auth for Next.js
sources.claim: Never trust getSession() in server code; getClaims() validates the JWT signature against the project's published public keys every time and is the call used to protect pages and data; the server function is the only checkpoint that always runs and must authorize the request itself.

sources.title: JWT signing keys
sources.claim: The original single shared secret is no longer recommended and kept for backward compatibility; with an asymmetric signing key JWT validation is local and fast and does not involve the Auth server.

sources.title: Going into production
sources.claim: Auth email rate limit is 2 emails per hour and can only be changed with a custom SMTP setup; OTP expiry recommended at 3600 seconds or lower; enterprise mail scanners can consume single-use links before the user clicks them.

sources.title: Redirect URLs
sources.claim: redirectTo must match the allowlist; wildcards including globstar are supported but exact redirect paths are recommended in production; Site URL is the default when no redirectTo is given.

sources.title: Supabase CLI config reference
sources.claim: Documented [auth] defaults, including enable_confirmations false, jwt_expiry 3600, refresh token rotation enabled with a 10s reuse interval, unset session timebox and inactivity_timeout, and MFA disabled.

sources.title: Branching — configuration as code
sources.claim: config.toml settings sync to branches on push, and a [remotes] block keyed by project id declares settings for a specific persistent project.

sources.title: @supabase/ssr type definitions (0.12.6, as installed)
sources.claim: setAll receives cookies and a headers object; responses that set auth cookies must not be cached by CDNs or reverse proxies, otherwise one user's session token can be served to a different user; cache headers arrive only with the first cookie write, so a new server client must be created per request; getClaims must be called before the response is generated.

sources.title: proxy.js file convention
sources.claim: Middleware is deprecated and renamed to Proxy in v16.0.0, defaulting to the Node.js runtime; a matcher that excludes a path also skips Server Function calls on that path, so a refactor can silently remove coverage; authentication and authorization must be verified inside each Server Function.

sources.title: How to think about data security in Next.js
sources.claim: An exported Server Action is reachable by direct POST even if never imported; a page-level authentication check does not extend to the Server Actions defined within it; the Data Access Layer performs authorization and returns minimal DTOs.

sources.title: GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw — Authorization Bypass in Next.js Middleware
sources.claim: CVSS 9.1; authorization can be bypassed if the check occurs in middleware, via the x-middleware-subrequest header; patched in 12.3.5/13.5.9/14.2.25/15.2.3; deployments hosted on Vercel are automatically protected.

sources.title: Password security
sources.claim: Leaked password protection uses the HaveIBeenPwned Pwned Passwords API and is available on the Pro Plan and above. Vendor documentation, but read here for plan availability rather than for a security claim.

sources.title: Understanding CVE-2025-29927
sources.claim: Practitioner analysis of how the header was exploited. Used to orient only; every asserted fact is cited to the advisory.

sources.title: RLS performance and best practices
sources.claim: Index columns used in RLS (>100x, 171ms to under 0.1ms); wrap functions in a select so the optimizer caches the result (179ms to 9ms, and 178,000ms to 12ms); ADD EXPLICIT FILTERS IN APPLICATION QUERIES ALONGSIDE RLS rather than relying on policies to filter (171ms to 9ms); use security-definer functions to avoid cascading policy evaluation on joins (9,000ms to 20ms); always specify `to authenticated`.

sources.title: Custom Claims & Role-based Access Control
sources.claim: The recommended RBAC pattern reads the role from the JWT in an authorize() function used by policies. The page does NOT state what a user must do after a role changes for the new claim to take effect — the staleness window is not mentioned.

sources.title: User sessions
sources.claim: Access tokens are short lived, usually between 5 minutes and 1 hour; refresh tokens never expire but are single-use. A claim written into an access token is therefore stale for up to the token lifetime.

sources.title: usebasejump/basejump
sources.claim: MIT by the text of LICENSE.md (GitHub's detector reports none). 940 stars. 19 .sql files against 2 .ts/.tsx and 13 `create policy` statements — a Postgres extension with a thin template. Last tagged release v2.0.3 on 2024-01-14; two commits since 2024-09-01, HEAD a merge dated 2026-08-06.

sources.title: Basejump's pgTAP suite
sources.claim: 13 pgTAP files covering schema, personal and team accounts, invitations, member removal, roles and billing functions. Adversarial rather than happy-path: 42 throws_ok assertions across at least eight identities switched via tests.authenticate_as(), asserting exact RLS refusal messages, including anonymous and cross-user attempts. No access matrix, no published per-table result, no badge, and the string `mutation` appears nowhere in the repository.

sources.title: Basejump CI workflow
sources.claim: Runs `supabase test db` on pull_request only, so a direct push to main is unverified, and pins supabase/setup-cli@v1 at `version: latest`. The single run the GitHub API still returns (2026-08-06) was CANCELLED — no verdict — and the pull request was merged.

sources.title: usebasejump/supabase-test-helpers
sources.claim: Separate repository, 131 stars, last pushed 2024-05-15, distributed through database.dev — test tooling published for other projects to use.

sources.title: supajump/supajump
sources.claim: 17 stars, last commit 2025-12-11. 72 `create policy` statements across 15 SQL files. Zero tests of any kind: no *.test.*, no *.spec.*, and `plan(` appears in no SQL file. Only workflows are claude.yml and claude-code-review.yml. No LICENSE file and no license field in package.json, so the default is all rights reserved.

sources.title: Upgrading Ruby on Rails
sources.claim: `bin/rails app:update` runs an INTERACTIVE session prompting per file (`Overwrite …? [Ynaqdh]`); diff/merge tools are pluggable via THOR_DIFF/THOR_MERGE. The guide does not classify files as framework-owned vs application-owned. New behaviour ships as a new file per version, config/initializers/new_framework_defaults_X_Y.rb.

sources.title: Expo — Prebuild / Continuous Native Generation
sources.claim: android/ and ios/ are generated from config and treated as short-lived. 'If you modify the generated directories manually then you risk losing your changes the next time you run npx expo prebuild --clean. Instead, use config plugins.' --clean warns on uncommitted changes because it deletes and recreates the native projects.

sources.title: Next.js — Codemods
sources.claim: Codemods apply breaking-API changes programmatically. Where an automatic migration is not possible the codemod inserts a comment or typecast and 'Your build will error until these comments are explicitly removed' — a transform that cannot finish fails loudly rather than half-applying.

sources.title: MakerKit — Clone the repository
sources.claim: Documents an `upstream` remote and `git pull upstream main`, advising it be run regularly. The page does not mention merge conflicts at all; the only warned failure is forgetting to run the package install afterwards.

sources.title: supastarter — Update the codebase
sources.claim: Upgrade is `git pull upstream main --allow-unrelated-histories --rebase`. Their own words: 'with every change you make to your application, it will become harder to update your code base, because you are essentially rebasing your code on top of the latest supastarter code with Git' and 'If you have any merge conflicts, you will have to resolve them manually.'

sources.title: Stripe — Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint
sources.claim: 'Stripe doesn't guarantee the delivery of events in the order that they're generated.' 'Don't use created to determine event order or whether you've already processed an event. Track event IDs to identify duplicate deliveries instead.' 'Webhook endpoints might occasionally receive the same event more than once.' 'Stripe attempts to deliver events to your destination for up to three days with an exponential back off in live mode.' Endpoints must return 2xx before complex logic, and signature verification uses the raw body with a default 5-minute timestamp tolerance.

sources.title: Stripe — Entitlements
sources.claim: Features attach to products; entitlements.active_entitlement_summary.updated fires when a customer's entitlements change; List Active Entitlements retrieves them on demand, recommended 'on application startup, for authorization checks, or to reconcile state after a webhook delivery failure'. Stripe's explicit recommendation: 'We recommend you persist these entitlements internally for faster resolution.' The summary webhook's entitlements.data array is capped at 10 — beyond that the payload's entitlements.url must be paginated, so a handler treating data as complete silently revokes the rest.

sources.title: Stripe — How subscriptions work
sources.claim: The status vocabulary and the grant/revoke boundary, in Stripe's words. trialing: 'The subscription is currently in a trial period and you can safely provision your product for your customer.' unpaid: 'Revoke access to your product when the subscription is unpaid because payments were already attempted and retried while past_due.' 'To move the subscription to active, pay the most recent invoice before its due date.' past_due: 'If the invoice is still unpaid after all attempted smart retries, you can configure the subscription to move to canceled, unpaid, or leave it as past_due.' canceled: 'This is a terminal state that can't be updated' and 'If your customer wants to resubscribe, you need to collect new payment information from them and create a new subscription.' paused: reachable only when a trial ends with no default payment method and trial_settings.end_behavior.missing_payment_method is pause. Delayed-confirmation methods (ACH): 'a subscription can move directly to active after creation and bypass incomplete. If the payment fails later, Stripe voids the invoice but the subscription remains active.' 'Voided invoices don't affect subscription status.'

sources.title: NN/g — Why You Only Need to Test with 5 Users
sources.claim: Problems found = N(1 - (1 - L)^n) with L about 31%. 'A single user uncovers roughly one-third of all problems'; by the fifth 'you are wasting your time by observing the same findings repeatedly'. Recommends several small studies over one large one: 'Spend this budget on 3 studies with 5 users each!'

sources.title: NN/g — Thinking Aloud: The #1 Usability Tool
sources.claim: Facilitator interference is the main threat: 'from an untrained facilitator, such interruptions can very easily change user behavior … the resulting behavior doesn't represent real use, so you can't base design decisions on the outcome.' The method is nonetheless robust — 'unless you blatantly bias users by putting words into their mouths, you'll still get reasonably good findings.'
